description: Make the public chat widget render bot replies with CLICKABLE links, XSS-safe by construction (escape-first-then-linkify with safeUrl). Currently Public/frontend/script.js appendChatMsg does `div.textContent = text;` for every bubble, so a Markdown link like `[Download](https://…/receipt.pdf)` or a bare URL is shown as raw plain text. Fix the bot bubble ONLY to linkify safely; user + error bubbles stay textContent. Dependency-free (this file is not bundled). Add a behavioral linkify test in mgmt/backend/test/frontend-medium-batch.test.mjs (the only harness that exercises Public/frontend source).
steps: In Public/frontend/script.js, add a pure, self-contained helper `linkifyBotText(text, escapeHtml, safeUrl)` near appendChatMsg (or just above it). It takes the raw model reply plus the existing escapeHtml/safeUrl helpers as INJECTED args (dependency injection makes it evaluable by the Node test without a DOM). Behavior, in this exact order: (1) FIRST run `escapeHtml(text)` over the ENTIRE reply so all HTML metacharacters (< > & " ') are neutralised — nothing the model returns can create markup. (2) THEN run a linkify regex over the ESCAPED string. Support Markdown links `[label](url)` and bare `https://…` / `http://…` URLs. Note: because escaping already happened, the regex matches the ESCAPED forms (e.g. the URL text has no raw < > so http(s):// URLs survive intact; a Markdown `[` `]` `(` `)` are not escaped by escapeHtml so `[label](url)` is still matchable). (3) For each matched URL, pass it through `safeUrl(url)` — if it returns '' (not http/https, e.g. javascript:/data:/vbscript:), DO NOT create a link: leave the already-escaped text as-is. If safeUrl returns a URL, build `${label}` where label is the already-escaped link text (for a bare URL, the label is the escaped URL string). (4) Return the resulting HTML string. Add a clear comment block explaining the escape-first-then-linkify ordering and WHY it is XSS-safe (escaping the whole string first means the only HTML that can ever exist in the output is the tags THIS function creates, with hrefs constrained to http(s) by safeUrl).

Handle the Markdown vs bare-URL matching carefully so a URL that is INSIDE a Markdown link is not double-linked. A single combined regex with alternation (Markdown-link branch first, then bare-URL branch) processed left-to-right via String.prototype.replace is the simplest correct approach. Keep the regex conservative: for the Markdown branch match `\[([^\]]+)\]\(([^)\s]+)\)`; for the bare-URL branch match `https?:\/\/[^\s<]+` and trim common trailing punctuation (. , ; : ) ] } ' ") off the matched URL so a sentence like 'see https://x/y.pdf.' does not swallow the period into the href.

In appendChatMsg, change ONLY the bot branch: when `kind` is 'bot' (i.e. not 'user' and not 'error'), set `div.innerHTML = linkifyBotText(text, escapeHtml, safeUrl);` with a comment that this is safe because linkifyBotText escapes the whole reply BEFORE building any markup and only emits <a> tags with safeUrl-validated http(s) hrefs. For 'user' and 'error' kinds, KEEP `div.textContent = text;` unchanged. Make the branch explicit so future readers see user/error stay textContent.

Add behavioral linkify tests to mgmt/backend/test/frontend-medium-batch.test.mjs (the existing frontend source-test harness — it already does `const read = (rel) => readFileSync(...)` and `read('../../../Public/frontend/script.js')`). Extract the three pure helpers (escapeHtml, safeUrl, linkifyBotText) from the source text and evaluate them in Node (e.g. slice each `function name(...) {...}` body out of src and build them with `new Function(...)`, or eval the concatenated three function sources into a scope) so the test exercises the REAL shipped logic, not a re-implementation. Cover, as separate assertions: (a) `[Download](https://x/y.pdf)` -> exactly `Download`; (b) a bare `https://files-chhath.shaharpura.com/2026/pdf/receipt-NCS-2026-64.pdf` becomes an whose href equals that URL; (c) a `[x](javascript:alert(1))` link and a bare `data:text/html,...` are NOT turned into and appear only as escaped text (assert the output contains no `` and `` is escaped (assert output contains `<img` / `<script` and NO literal `

Also add a source-level assertion (matching the existing L-19 style in the same file) that appendChatMsg's bot path uses linkifyBotText/innerHTML while the user+error paths still use textContent — so a future edit that naively reverts to a blanket textContent or that assigns raw text to innerHTML is caught.
Run the backend suite: `cd mgmt/backend && env -u NODE_OPTIONS npm test` and confirm all pass (>=600, plus the new linkify tests).
acceptance_criteria: appendChatMsg renders the 'bot' bubble via innerHTML using linkifyBotText(text, escapeHtml, safeUrl); 'user' and 'error' bubbles still use textContent.

linkifyBotText escapes the entire reply BEFORE linkifying and only emits <a> tags with http(s) hrefs validated by safeUrl; target="_blank" and rel="noopener noreferrer nofollow" are set on every emitted link.
javascript:/data:/vbscript: URLs are NOT linked and remain inert escaped text; raw HTML in the reply is escaped and cannot execute.
No new npm dependency or test framework is added; the file remains plain browser JS with no imports/exports.

New behavioral linkify tests exercise the REAL extracted functions and cover the Markdown-link, bare-URL, dangerous-scheme, HTML-injection, and plain-text cases; `cd mgmt/backend && env -u NODE_OPTIONS npm test` passes.
verification: cd mgmt/backend && env -u NODE_OPTIONS npm test
findings: Implemented app.linkifyBotText(text, escapeHtml, safeUrl) in Public/frontend/script.js (escape-first-then-linkify; Markdown [label](url) + bare http(s) URLs; safeUrl gates href to http(s); target=_blank rel=noopener noreferrer nofollow; trailing punctuation trimmed off bare URLs). appendChatMsg now renders ONLY the bot bubble via innerHTML; user+error stay textContent. Added 8 behavioral tests to mgmt/backend/test/frontend-medium-batch.test.mjs that extract and run the REAL escapeHtml/safeUrl/linkifyBotText from source. NOTE: the test's function-slice helper cannot use naive brace counting for linkifyBotText because its body has { } inside a regex character class ([.,;:)\]}...]); it anchors on the following appendChatMsg method instead. node --check passes; backend suite 608 pass / 0 fail (600 baseline + 8 new).
